newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends stronger after U.S. labor data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends stronger after U.S. labor data.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended stronger on Thursday at C$1.3738 (US$0.7279) in steady trade after the U.S. Department of Labor reported an increase of 217,000 in non-farm payrolls for June, slightly below expectations, traders said.
* They said traders would likely consolidate their gains and trade would be limited on Friday for the U.S. July 4 holiday.
"The street is probably a little bit long Canada right now, so before the long weekend they're erasing some positions," said a trader at a Canadian bank.
Traders said the U.S. payrolls report would likely add more strength to the Canadian dollar next week after the Federal Reserve left U.S. rates unchanged this week.
The Fed Reserve decided at the end of its Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Wednesday that the slowdown justified leaving U.S. interest rates unchanged.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar dipped to 82.72 Japanese yen from Wednesday's 83.19 yen but held steady around 1.2754 marks.
